# Coder protocol: no hardwiring, and how to read a failing check

## The one rule (the owner's, verbatim — it governs everything below)

> NO HARDWIRING. A failing case is never fixed by name. No per-case branches,
> no literal document strings, no test-case IDs, no rescue functions, no
> per-case switches. Find the general cause and fix the mechanism so every
> case of that kind passes. If you cannot find a general fix, say so and stop
> — a pass patch is a failure, not progress.

The gate has teeth: a fix is accepted only if it holds on inputs you have
never seen. CI rejects a diff that adds `_rescue_*`, `*_NEEDLES`, `*_RESCUE`
knobs, or a probe or test-case ID inside product code. "Loop until every
test passes" is not your order; passing the tests you can see is not the
target — working on the ones you cannot see is.

## Four tests for whether what you wrote is variable by design

1. **No named cases in production code.** If a probe ID, a test-case name, a
   specific document string, or one customer's values appears in the shipped
   path, it is a fixed point wearing a variable-shaped wrapper.
2. **It passes on inputs it has never seen — by construction, not by luck.**
   If the only cases it clears are the ones you tuned on, the variability is
   an illusion.
3. **Every fix is general, or it is rejected.** A change that makes one case
   pass and cannot be justified as a class-level fix does not ship.
4. **Contracts, not answers.** A capability declares what it accepts and the
   shape it produces — on the spec (`allowed_values`, types, bounds) — and
   never the specific values it expects. Shape is enforced; values flow
   through.

## How to read a failing check

A failing check says the product is not yet doing what the brief asked, at
the bar the brief set. Fix the cause. Never make the test, or the product's
own validation, agree to accept wrong input.

1. Read the `FAILED` line and its message. A vocabulary error names the field
   and the values the route accepts (`... must be one of: a, b, c`).
2. Decide which side is wrong:
   - The route is **right** to refuse a value outside its declared vocabulary.
     The fix is to declare that vocabulary on the spec field so a payload built
     from the spec is one the route accepts — not to make the route accept
     anything.
   - The route is **wrong** only if it refuses a value the brief defines as
     valid. Then fix the handler, and keep every other check.
3. If the message says the tester **already tried the values the route named**
   and the route still refused, the product contradicts itself: two layers
   (route guard, handler, block) disagree about the same field. Reconcile them.
   Do not delete either blindly.
4. If the general cause is not there to be found, say so and stop. That is a
   valid outcome. A patch is not.

## The bar is the brief's, not a fixed one

Never weaken, delete, or loosen a validation, a route check, or a test
assertion **below the bar the brief set**. If the brief asked for a prototype,
prototype-level checks are the bar, and meeting it is not cheating; if the
brief asked for pilot, pilot is the bar. What is never allowed is buying a
green by removing a check the brief required — that is a red you hid, and the
next gate finds it.

## What counts as a pass patch — do none of these

- Deleting or commenting out a validation branch so bad input passes.
- Widening an enum, or dropping it, to swallow a test's placeholder value.
- Replacing a real assertion with `assert True`, `pytest.skip`, or `xfail`.
- Catching an exception and returning `ok: true` to mask it.
- Hardcoding a test's expected output inside the handler.
- A branch, a string match, or a lookup keyed on one case so that case passes.

## What a real fix looks like

- The contract on the spec matches what the handler enforces, so a payload
  built from the spec is one the handler accepts.
- The handler does the work the brief describes and returns real results, for
  any valid input of that kind — not for the inputs you happened to see.
- Every check the brief required is still there after the fix.

# Coder protocol: no hardwiring, and how to read a failing check

## The one rule (the owner's, verbatim — it governs everything below)

> NO HARDWIRING. A failing case is never fixed by name. No per-case branches,
> no literal document strings, no test-case IDs, no rescue functions, no
> per-case switches. Find the general cause and fix the mechanism so every
> case of that kind passes. If you cannot find a general fix, say so and stop
> — a pass patch is a failure, not progress.

The gate has teeth: a fix is accepted only if it holds on inputs you have
never seen. CI rejects a diff that adds `_rescue_*`, `*_NEEDLES`, `*_RESCUE`
knobs, or a probe or test-case ID inside product code. "Loop until every
test passes" is not your order; passing the tests you can see is not the
target — working on the ones you cannot see is.

## Four tests for whether what you wrote is variable by design

1. **No named cases in production code.** If a probe ID, a test-case name, a
   specific document string, or one customer's values appears in the shipped
   path, it is a fixed point wearing a variable-shaped wrapper.
2. **It passes on inputs it has never seen — by construction, not by luck.**
   If the only cases it clears are the ones you tuned on, the variability is
   an illusion.
3. **Every fix is general, or it is rejected.** A change that makes one case
   pass and cannot be justified as a class-level fix does not ship.
4. **Contracts, not answers.** A capability declares what it accepts and the
   shape it produces — on the spec (`allowed_values`, types, bounds) — and
   never the specific values it expects. Shape is enforced; values flow
   through.

## How to read a failing check

A failing check says the product is not yet doing what the brief asked, at
the bar the brief set. Fix the cause. Never make the test, or the product's
own validation, agree to accept wrong input.

1. Read the `FAILED` line and its message. A vocabulary error names the field
   and the values the route accepts (`... must be one of: a, b, c`).
2. Decide which side is wrong:
   - The route is **right** to refuse a value outside its declared vocabulary.
     The fix is to declare that vocabulary on the spec field so a payload built
     from the spec is one the route accepts — not to make the route accept
     anything.
   - The route is **wrong** only if it refuses a value the brief defines as
     valid. Then fix the handler, and keep every other check.
3. If the message says the tester **already tried the values the route named**
   and the route still refused, the product contradicts itself: two layers
   (route guard, handler, block) disagree about the same field. Reconcile them.
   Do not delete either blindly.
4. If the general cause is not there to be found, say so and stop. That is a
   valid outcome. A patch is not.

## The bar is the brief's, not a fixed one

Never weaken, delete, or loosen a validation, a route check, or a test
assertion **below the bar the brief set**. If the brief asked for a prototype,
prototype-level checks are the bar, and meeting it is not cheating; if the
brief asked for pilot, pilot is the bar. What is never allowed is buying a
green by removing a check the brief required — that is a red you hid, and the
next gate finds it.

## What counts as a pass patch — do none of these

- Deleting or commenting out a validation branch so bad input passes.
- Widening an enum, or dropping it, to swallow a test's placeholder value.
- Replacing a real assertion with `assert True`, `pytest.skip`, or `xfail`.
- Catching an exception and returning `ok: true` to mask it.
- Hardcoding a test's expected output inside the handler.
- A branch, a string match, or a lookup keyed on one case so that case passes.

## What a real fix looks like

- The contract on the spec matches what the handler enforces, so a payload
  built from the spec is one the handler accepts.
- The handler does the work the brief describes and returns real results, for
  any valid input of that kind — not for the inputs you happened to see.
- Every check the brief required is still there after the fix.

def _refresh_factory_files(self) -> None:
        from app.factory.build.factory_refresh import product_display_name, refresh_factory_files

        name = product_display_name(self.blueprint)
        try:
            changed = refresh_factory_files(
                self.workspace, name, self.blueprint
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- recorded; the gates still judge
            self.ledger.append(
                EventKind.NOTE,
                detail=f"factory file refresh failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                payload={"refresh_failed": True},
            )
            return
        if changed:
            self.ledger.append(
                EventKind.NOTE,
                detail="REFRESHED factory files from current templates: " + ", ".join(changed),
                payload={"refreshed": changed},
            )

    def _factory_test_files(self) -> list:
        """Test files TESTER itself wrote -- the tests the WRITER may not edit.

        From this run's state, else the ledger (a resume, or a pilot cycle
        that kept the suite), so ownership survives a process restart.
        """
        files = self.state.get("factory_test_files")
        if files:
            return list(files)
        events = list(self.ledger.events()) if self.ledger.exists() else []
        for event in reversed(events):
            recorded = (event.payload or {}).get("factory_test_files")
            if recorded:
                return list(recorded)
        return []

    def _behavior_test_files(self) -> list:
        """Tests run_tester's own emitters stamped -- assertions in these
        judge the PRODUCT by construction. From state, else the ledger,
        exactly like _factory_test_files, so ownership survives a resume."""
        files = self.state.get("behavior_test_files")
        if files:
            return list(files)
        events = list(self.ledger.events()) if self.ledger.exists() else []
        for event in reversed(events):
            payload = event.payload or {}
            if payload.get("behavior_test_files"):
                return list(payload["behavior_test_files"])
        return []

    def _run_phase(self, role: BuildRole, work_list: Sequence[str]) -> GateResult:
        """Run the role then its gate. Raises RoleError / AuthorityError up."""
        self.ledger.append(EventKind.PHASE_STARTED, role=role, detail=role.value)
        logger.info("phase start: role=%s", role.value)
        # The WRITER is staged: it rewrites app/ wholesale on every rework
        # round, and the agent picks different entity names each call, so a
        # pass killed part-way through would leave models.py from one attempt
        # beside routes.py from another. Observed live as
        # "no such table: field_defect". Other roles append rather than
        # replace, so a partial pass is recoverable by re-running them.
        staging = (
            self.workspace.parent / f".{self.workspace.name}.staging-{role.value.lower()}"
            if role is BuildRole.WRITER
            else None
        )
        if staging is not None and staging.exists():
            # A staging tree at phase start means the previous WRITER pass
            # died mid-way (a committed pass removes its own staging). It
            # used to be wiped unconditionally -- right for the in-process
            # coder, which rewrites app/ wholesale and picks new entity names
            # each call. The CodeWhale agent is different: it narrates every
            # step to docs/writer_progress.log, so it can read where it got
            # to and carry on. Wiping threw away a finished 17-step pass
            # because the server restarted 25 seconds after it (live).
            if self._writer_can_resume(staging):
                self.state["writer_resumed"] = True
                self.ledger.append(
                    EventKind.NOTE,

                    detail=(

                        "progress log are kept; the agent continues, it does "

            """Record intra-phase progress as a ledger NOTE.

            NOTE deliberately: it is not a verdict, so completed_roles(),
            resume_point() and the terminal-event readers are untouched -- a
            progress line can never be mistaken for a gate result.

"""Local block dispatch. No network, no store, no callback.

The old generated platforms answered a capability by POSTing to the operator's
block store. This imports the block that was vendored into this repository at
build time and calls it in-process, which is what makes the platform runnable
offline and independent of the factory's uptime.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

_VENDOR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "vendor" / "blocks"
_CACHE: Dict[str, Any] = {}


class BlockNotVendored(RuntimeError):
    """Asked for a block this platform does not carry."""


def load_block(block_id: str):
    if block_id in _CACHE:
        return _CACHE[block_id]
    path = _VENDOR / block_id / "block.py"
    if not path.is_file():
        raise BlockNotVendored(
            f"{block_id} is not vendored in this platform (looked in {path})"
        )
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(f"vendored_{block_id}", path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    _CACHE[block_id] = module
    return module

"""Re-write the Factory's own files on a re-entered build.

A build resumed from an earlier run -- or attached from its cerebrum-builds
branch -- carries the Factory files of the Factory that FIRST built it. When
the Factory has since been fixed, those old copies keep failing the build:
live, a hotel platform built before the release-gate fix kept a
``scripts/release_gate.py`` that demands a withheld file, so every resume
failed its Docker image at 0/13 no matter how green the product was.

So on re-entry, before TESTER, the files the Factory owns outright are
re-rendered from the CURRENT templates. Only files that are pure Factory
templates with no coder content; the coder's files (handlers, models, routes,
dispatch) are never touched.

requirements.txt is MERGED, never replaced: every line the build declares
(a Postgres driver, say) stays, and only the vendored blocks' missing
obligations are added.

Before #683 the Factory appended its lines UNMARKED, under
``LEGACY_BLOCK_HEADER``, once per refresh. Those lines are the Factory's, not
the product's, but the marker reader cannot tell -- so a branch of record kept
every package an older Factory ever stamped, for blocks it no longer vendors
(live 2026-10-07: ``marker-pdf`` pinned ``pillow<11`` into a vineyard image
that imports neither, and 33 pillow advisories were billed to the writer).
The merge removes those legacy blocks and re-derives the Factory's lines into
its marked block, so a stale Factory line goes with the stamp that owns it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, List

_LF = "\n"


def _dist(line: str):
    text = line.strip()
    if not text or text.startswith("#"):
        return None
    return re.split(r"[<>=!~\[; ]", text, 1)[0].strip().lower().replace("_", "-")


def _write_if_changed(
    root: Path, rel: str, text: str, changed: List[str], *, shared: bool = False
) -> None:
    """Write ``text`` when it differs. A Factory-owned file is normalised to
    LF; a SHARED file (``shared=True``) is written exactly as given, so the
    product's own bytes -- line endings included -- are never rewritten."""
    path = root / rel
    if not shared:
        text = text.replace("\r\n", _LF)
    old = path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8") if path.is_file() else None
    if old is not None and not shared:
        old = old.replace("\r\n", _LF)
    if old == text:
        return
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
    changed.append(rel)


#: The header the pre-#683 merge emitted above each unmarked block of
#: Factory lines (git show 588ab537^:backend/app/factory/build/factory_refresh.py).
#: The Factory's own former output, read only to remove it.
LEGACY_BLOCK_HEADER = (
    "# Packages this tree needs and did not declare: vendored block\n"
    "# imports, and framework features FastAPI does not declare\n"
    "# (refreshed by the factory)."
)


def strip_legacy_blocks(text: str) -> str:
    """``text`` without the unmarked blocks the pre-#683 Factory appended.

    That emitter wrote a blank line, ``LEGACY_BLOCK_HEADER``, then one
    requirement line per package -- and nothing else -- so a block ends at the
    first blank or comment line. Every other byte is returned as it was.
    """
    header = LEGACY_BLOCK_HEADER.split(_LF)
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    out: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        window = [line.rstrip("\r\n") for line in lines[i:i + len(header)]]
        if window != header:
            out.append(lines[i])
            i += 1
            continue
        if out and not out[-1].strip():
            out.pop()  # the blank line the emitter put before its header
        i += len(header)
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and not lines[i].lstrip().startswith("#"):
            i += 1
    return "".join(out)

    """Write health, observability, revision identity, rollback, deploy doc."""
    for rel, content in deploy_substrate():

def deploy_substrate() -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:

    The third emitter stranded below ``run_writer``'s CodeWhale branch, and so
    never run in production, while ``run_tester`` stamps

# Vineyard Management Platform -- one image, no outbound dependency at runtime.
#
# The build context is a deliverable: it does NOT run the test suite, the
# release gate, or any dev dependency. Python-only, deterministic given the same
# sources. The console the image serves at "/" is the built asset committed at

# PLATFORM_CURRENCY reach the process from the deploy environment only, never
# from a file in this context, and never from an ENV line below.
FROM python:3.11-slim

    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \

"""HTTP surface for the Vineyard Management Platform.

Written by the factory WRITER role (codewhale exec).

Every /v1 route is authenticated (401 with no token), every validation
failure is a 4xx naming the field, and only a declared vocabulary is
accepted.  The ROUTE owns the tenant-scoped save: a handler never persists.
Tenancy is resolved from the bearer token, never from the payload.  A
capability whose connector is a declared placeholder answers the typed 503
refusal before validation and before its handler runs; nothing is stored.

Reads answer with the capability's authority label, so an operator (and the
console) can see which layer of precedence.v1 answered.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from app import store
from app.auth import (
    reject_invalid_payload,
    reject_reserved_payload_keys,
    require_platform_token,
    require_read_token,
)
from app.edge import reject_wrong_types

from fastapi import Depends
from app.jobs import CATALOG, GATES, JOBS
from app.models import MODELS
from app.tenancy import bind_tenant, release_tenant

router = APIRouter()

#: The capability roster is app.models.MODELS -- the platform's own single
#: declaration (entity name == capability id).
CAPABILITY_IDS = sorted(MODELS)
#: The store entity each capability's route saves to.  The one-record
#: round-trip probe reads this back, so it names the migration's table.
ENTITY_OF = {cap: getattr(cls, "ENTITY", cap) for cap, cls in sorted(MODELS.items())}
ROUTE_ENTITIES = dict(ENTITY_OF)

#: The authority layer each capability's answers carry -- the same label its
#: handler stamps on a POST answer.  A READ answer is the platform's record
#: of that capability, so it answers at the same layer.
READ_AUTHORITY: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {
    "fermentation_tank_tracking": {"layer": 3, "name": "formulas", "source": "app/formulas.py"},
    "harvest_scheduling_sugar_readings": {"layer": 3, "name": "formulas", "source": "app/formulas.py"},
    "barrel_inventory_two_cellars": {"layer": 3, "name": "formulas", "source": "app/formulas.py"},
    "club_member_shipments": {"layer": 3, "name": "formulas", "source": "app/formulas.py"},
    "vintage_lot_traceability": {"layer": 2, "name": "documents", "source": "app/actions/vintage_lot_traceability.py"},
    "cellar_operations_workbench": {"layer": 3, "name": "formulas", "source": "app/formulas.py"},
    "compliance_and_label_governance": {"layer": 1, "name": "certified", "source": "app/actions/compliance_and_label_governance.py"},
}

#: Query parameters a list route understands beside the declared columns.
LIST_CONTROLS = ("limit", "offset", "sort", "order")


def _require_identity(request: Request) -> None:
    """Resolve the caller's tenant as a DEPENDENCY, before anything else.

    FastAPI validates a route's typed body and path parameters in the same
    pass as its dependencies, but sub-dependencies are solved first: making
    the token check a dependency means an anonymous caller gets 401 even
    when the body is not an object or the id is not a number, instead of a
    422 that confirms the route exists.
    """
    require_platform_token(request)


def _placeholder_refusal(cap_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """The typed 503 for a capability whose connector is a declared placeholder."""
    try:
        from app import placeholders
    except ImportError:
        return None
    return placeholders.refusal_for(cap_id)


def _run(cap_id: str, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    module = importlib.import_module("app.actions." + cap_id)
    return module.handle(payload)


def _labelled(capability_id: str, body: Any) -> Any:
    """Attach the capability's authority label to one read answer."""
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        return body
    out = dict(body)
    label = READ_AUTHORITY.get(str(capability_id))
    if label is not None and "authority" not in out:
        out["authority"] = dict(label)
    return out


def _error(cap_id: str, exc: Exception) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "ok": False,
        "capability": cap_id,
        "error": "%s: %s" % (type(exc).__name__, exc),
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kernel job routes (read-only)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
@router.get("/jobs")
def list_jobs(request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    require_read_token(request)
    return {"jobs": JOBS}


@router.get("/catalog")
def catalog(request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    require_read_token(request)
    return CATALOG

def inventory(request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    require_read_token(request)
    from app import jobs

    require_read_token(request)

    for entry in (CATALOG.get("bindings") or []):

    items = []
    for cap_id, cls in sorted(MODELS.items()):

        item = {

        item["fields"] = list(getattr(cls, "FIELDS", []) or [])
        item["constraints"] = dict(getattr(cls, "CONSTRAINTS", {}) or {})
        item["money_fields"] = list(getattr(cls, "MONEY_FIELDS", []) or [])
        item["entity"] = getattr(cls, "ENTITY", cap_id)
        item["authority"] = dict(READ_AUTHORITY.get(cap_id) or {})
        item["http"] = {
            "create": "POST /v1/%s" % cap_id,
            "list": "GET /v1/%s" % cap_id,
            "get": "GET /v1/%s/{id}" % cap_id,
            "update": "PUT /v1/%s/{id}" % cap_id,
            "delete": "DELETE /v1/%s/{id}" % cap_id,

        try:

            item["placeholder"] = bool(placeholders.PLACEHOLDER_CONNECTORS.get(cap_id))
            item["placeholder_settings"] = [
                placeholders.setting_for(c)
                for c in (placeholders.PLACEHOLDER_CONNECTORS.get(cap_id) or [])
            ]
        except ImportError:
            item["placeholder"] = False
        items.append(item)
    return {"items": items}


@router.get("/gates")
def gates(request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    require_read_token(request)
    return GATES


@router.get("/provenance")
def provenance(request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    require_read_token(request)
    from app import jobs

    return jobs.provenance()


@router.get("/authority")
def authority_layers(request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """precedence.v1 as data: the layers an answer's label indexes into."""
    require_read_token(request)
    from app import authority

    return authority.precedence_table()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Capability CRUD.  One set of handlers per capability, registered on the
# router by name at import; every write is tenant-scoped from the bearer
# token and every refusal is 4xx or ok:false with a reason, never a 500.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _make_create(cap_id: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    entity = ENTITY_OF[cap_id]

    async def create(payload: Dict[str, Any], request: Request) -> Any:
        tenant = require_platform_token(request)
        reject_reserved_payload_keys(payload)
        refusal = _placeholder_refusal(cap_id)
        if refusal is not None:
            return JSONResponse(status_code=503, content=refusal)
        reject_invalid_payload(cap_id, payload)
        reject_wrong_types(cap_id, payload)
        [redacted]
        try:
            try:
                answer = _run(cap_id, payload)
            except Exception as exc:  # a handler refusal is an answer, not a 500
                answer = _error(cap_id, exc)
        finally:
            release_tenant(token)
        if not isinstance(answer, dict):
            answer = {
                "ok": False,
                "capability": cap_id,
                "error": "handle() returned a non-mapping",
            }
        if answer.get("ok") is False:
            return answer
        columns = store.COLUMNS.get(entity, [])
        record = {k: v for k, v in payload.items() if k in columns}
        try:
            stored = store.save(entity, record, tenant.tenant_id)
        except Exception as exc:  # a store refusal is a refusal, not a 500
            return _error(cap_id, exc)
        merged = dict(answer)
        merged.setdefault("ok", True)
        merged["capability"] = cap_id
        merged["stored"] = stored
        #: The record's own id at the top level: a reader (and the factory's
        #: round-trip probe) must not have to search the block evidence below
        #: for the id of the row the route just persisted.
        merged["id"] = stored.get("id")
        merged["record_id"] = stored.get("id")
        return merged

    create.__name__ = "%s_create" % cap_id
    return create


def _make_list(cap_id: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    entity = ENTITY_OF[cap_id]

    def list_records(request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        tenant = require_read_token(request)
        allowed = set(store.COLUMNS.get(entity, [])) | set(LIST_CONTROLS)
        given = dict(request.query_params)
        unknown = sorted(k for k in given if k not in allowed)
        if unknown:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=422, detail="unknown query field(s): " + ", ".join(unknown)
            )
        try:
            limit = int(given.get("limit", 50))
            offset = int(given.get("offset", 0))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="limit/offset must be integers")
        try:
            return _labelled(
                cap_id,
                store.query(
                    entity, tenant.tenant_id,
                    filters={k: v for k, v in given.items() if k not in LIST_CONTROLS},
                    sort=given.get("sort"),
                    order=given.get("order", "asc"),
                    limit=limit,
                    offset=offset,
                ),
            )
        except (store.QueryError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=str(exc))

status vocabulary is schema-enforced here (open | in_progress | closed),
never described in prose.

code and no rate is a literal anywhere in this source: every amount would be
read from app.money_settings at the point of use, and while no currency is
declared the money leg is reported as withheld rather than invented. This
build declares no money field.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

#: The envelope vocabulary every capability shares. Enforced on the spec by
#: CONSTRAINTS (allowed_values), so a status outside it is refused by the
#: route with 422 -- the schema is the contract, not a comment.
ENVELOPE_STATUS = ["open", "in_progress", "closed"]

#: The two cellars this winery ages in. A cellar outside the vocabulary is
#: refused by name rather than stored as free text.
CELLARS = ["cellar_a", "cellar_b"]

#: import, from APPROVED_PRINCIPALS (comma-separated); ``unset`` stands for
#: "the operator has configured no principal yet", so the vocabulary is
#: never empty and no name is invented in place of a real principal.
APPROVED_PRINCIPALS = [
    name.strip()
    for name in (os.environ.get("APPROVED_PRINCIPALS") or "").split(",")

"""Handler for capability fermentation_tank_tracking.

One fermentation tank, its latest reading and the state it is in. The
winemaker's decision this record supports: a tank whose sugar is not falling
is a stalled fermentation and needs attention before it spoils.

The stall threshold is the winery's setting (WINERY_STALL_BRIX_PER_DAY),
read here and never typed into this module.

This capability's connectors (tank_sensor_gateway, winery_lab_system) are
declared placeholders, so its route answers the typed 503 refusal before
this handler runs and nothing is stored; the handler is written as it will
work once those connectors exist.

Scope READS: caller input, app.tenancy (the bound principal), operator
settings from the environment, the vendored blocks this capability
declares. Scope WRITES: caller output only.
Scope NEVER: no network, no store callback, no direct store write, no
reading invented for a tank nobody sampled.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from app import formulas
from app.actions._blocks import call_blocks

AUTHORED_BY = "codewhale exec"

CAPABILITY_ID = "fermentation_tank_tracking"
ENTITY = "fermentation_tank_tracking"
BLOCK_IDS = ["dashboard", "notification", "analytics"]
#: Each bound block's own declared default: dashboard's is ``render``,
#: notification's is ``send`` (driven through the block's own ``outbox``
#: operation -- ``send`` needs the event_bus peer this vendor slice does not
#: carry, and a handler must not claim a delivery the platform cannot make),
#: analytics' is ``track_event``.
BLOCK_DEFAULT_ACTIONS = {
    "dashboard": "render",
    "notification": "outbox",
    "analytics": "track_event",
}
CAPABILITY_FIELDS = [
    "reference", "status", "tank_code", "variety", "lot_code", "stage",
    "brix", "temperature_c", "density", "volume_liters",
    "days_since_reading", "fill_date", "last_reading_at", "stalled", "notes",
]

STALL_THRESHOLD_ENV = "WINERY_STALL_BRIX_PER_DAY"
STALL_THRESHOLD_DEFAULT = 0.05


def _tenant() -> str:
    try:
        from app.tenancy import current_tenant_id

        return current_tenant_id() or "local"
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - tenancy may be unbound in-process
        return "local"


def _number(value: Any, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
    try:
        if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None or value == "":
            return default
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default


def stall_threshold() -> float:
    raw = (os.environ.get(STALL_THRESHOLD_ENV) or "").strip()
    if not raw:
        return STALL_THRESHOLD_DEFAULT
    try:
        value = float(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return STALL_THRESHOLD_DEFAULT
    return value if value >= 0 else STALL_THRESHOLD_DEFAULT


def analyse(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Whether the fermentation is moving, finishing, or stalled."""
    brix = _number(payload.get("brix"))
    previous = _number(payload.get("previous_brix"), brix)
    days = max(1, int(_number(payload.get("days_since_reading"), 1)))
    per_day = formulas.brix_drop_per_day(previous, brix, days)
    threshold = stall_threshold()
    temp_limit = formulas.tank_temperature_limit()
    stage = str(payload.get("stage") or "primary")
    stalled = bool(per_day < threshold and stage not in ("complete", "press"))
    return {
        "tank_code": str(payload.get("tank_code") or ""),
        "stage": stage,
        "brix": brix,
        "previous_brix": previous,
        "drop_per_day": round(per_day, 4),
        "stall_threshold": threshold,
        "stalled": stalled or bool(payload.get("stalled")),
        "temperature_c": _number(payload.get("temperature_c")),
        "temperature_limit_c": temp_limit,
        "running_warm": bool(_number(payload.get("temperature_c")) > temp_limit),
        "ready_to_press": bool(stage in ("press", "complete")),
        "summary": "tank %s: %.1f Brix, %.3f/day — %s" % (
            str(payload.get("tank_code") or ""), brix, per_day,
            "stalled" if stalled else "fermenting",
        ),
    }


def _block_inputs(payload: Dict[str, Any], analysis: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
    tenant = _tenant()
    reference = str(payload.get("reference") or analysis["tank_code"])
    record = {k: payload.get(k) for k in CAPABILITY_FIELDS}
    return {
        "dashboard": {
            "dashboard_id": ENTITY,
            "title": "Fermentation tanks",
            "widgets": [
                {"id": "brix", "type": "metric", "title": analysis["tank_code"], "value": analysis["brix"], "unit": "Brix"},
            ],
            "layout": {"columns": 2, "stage": analysis["stage"]},
        },
        "notification": {
            "message": analysis["summary"],
            "topic": "cellar/tank/%s" % (analysis["tank_code"] or "unknown"),
            "channel": "mcp",
            "payload": {
                "tank_code": analysis["tank_code"],
                "stalled": analysis["stalled"],
                "drop_per_day": analysis["drop_per_day"],
            },
            "tool": "event_bus",
            "principal_id": tenant,
            "reference": reference,
        },
        "analytics": {
            "metric": "fermentation_drop_per_day",
            "value": analysis["drop_per_day"],
            "dimensions": {"tank_code": analysis["tank_code"], "stage": analysis["stage"]},
        },
    }


def handle(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Answer with the tank's fermentation state, then drive every block."""
    payload = dict(payload or {})

This module owns the two contracts every handler keeps and nothing else --
each handler builds its own inputs and makes its own domain decision:

* every id in the handler's ``BLOCK_IDS`` is called, and a block refusal is
  returned as the capability's refusal -- ``ok: False`` with the refusing
  block named, and nothing persisted -- never reported as success (F1).

diagnosis, so it is recorded in the same shape rather than escaping as a

FAILED_STATUSES = ("error", "failed", "partial")


def is_refusal(envelope: Any) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(envelope, dict):
        return False
    if envelope.get("ok") is False:
        return True
    if str(envelope.get("status") or "").lower() in FAILED_STATUSES:

    steps = envelope.get("results")

        for step in steps:
            if isinstance(step, dict) and str(step.get("status") or "").lower() in FAILED_STATUSES:
                return True
    return False


def refusal_text(block_id: str, envelope: Any) -> str:
    if isinstance(envelope, dict):
        detail = envelope.get("error") or envelope.get("message")

"""Capabilities whose connectors are declared placeholders.

Written by the Factory from the blueprint.  A capability listed here
answers the typed unavailable refusal until its connector is built; every
other capability is expected to work.

This build declares three connectors on two capabilities:

* club_member_shipments -- payment_processor, shipping_carrier_api
* harvest_scheduling_sugar_readings     -- weather_api

The refusal is typed (HTTP 503, ``ok: false``, ``error_kind:
"unavailable"``) and names, for every connector, the environment setting the
operator must supply.  Nothing is stored for a refused capability: the route
answers before validation and before the handler runs, so a caller can never
mistake a placeholder for a working integration.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

UNAVAILABLE_KIND = "unavailable"
REFUSAL_LOG_ENV = "PLACEHOLDER_REFUSAL_LOG"
UNAVAILABLE_STATUS = 503
SETTING_SUFFIX = "_CREDENTIALS"

#: capability id -> the connectors the blueprint declares as placeholders.
PLACEHOLDER_CONNECTORS: Dict[str, List[str]] = {
    "fermentation_tank_tracking": ["tank_sensor_gateway", "winery_lab_system"],
    "harvest_scheduling_sugar_readings": ["vineyard_block_sensor_feed"],
    "club_member_shipments": ["shipping_carrier", "winery_club_crm"],
}


def setting_for(connector_id: str) -> str:
    return connector_id.upper() + SETTING_SUFFIX


def _record(capability_id: str) -> None:
    path = os.environ.get(REFUSAL_LOG_ENV)
    if not path:
        return
    running = os.environ.get("PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST") or ""
    test = running.rsplit(" (", 1)[0]
    try:
        with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps({"test": test, "capability": capability_id}) + "\n")
    except OSError:
        pass


def refusal_for(capability_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """The typed refusal for a declared capability, else None."""
    connectors = PLACEHOLDER_CONNECTORS.get(capability_id) or []
    if not connectors:
        return None
    _record(capability_id)
    settings = [setting_for(c) for c in connectors]
    return {
        "ok": False,
        "error_kind": UNAVAILABLE_KIND,
        "capability": capability_id,
        "connectors": list(connectors),
        "settings": settings,
        "error": "not configured: " + ", ".join(
            "%s is a placeholder connector (needs %s)" % (c, s)
            for c, s in zip(connectors, settings)
        ),
    }


def is_declared_refusal(capability_id: str, status_code: int, body: Any) -> bool:
    connectors = PLACEHOLDER_CONNECTORS.get(capability_id) or []
    return (
        bool(connectors)
        and status_code == UNAVAILABLE_STATUS
        and isinstance(body, dict)
        and body.get("ok") is False
        and body.get("error_kind") == UNAVAILABLE_KIND
        and list(body.get("settings") or []) == [setting_for(c) for c in connectors]
    )

"""Edge validation: a value must BE the type the capability declares.

The capability's own model is the contract: ``barrel_code: str`` means a
number is not a barrel code, ``vintage: int`` means a list is not a vintage,
``hold: bool`` means "yes" is not a decision. The route validates at the
edge, before the handler runs and before anything is stored, and answers 422
naming the field.

This is driven entirely by the model's declared annotations -- there is no
per-field or per-capability branch here, so a field added to a capability is
validated the moment it is declared.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import typing
from typing import Any, Dict

from fastapi import HTTPException

#: What each declared annotation accepts. ``None`` is always allowed for a
#: field the caller left out or explicitly nulled; the store holds NULL.
_ACCEPTS: Dict[str, tuple] = {
    "str": (str,),
    "int": (int,),
    "float": (int, float),
    "bool": (bool,),
}


def _declared_kind(annotation: Any) -> str:
    """The JSON kind a Python annotation names, or "" when it names none."""
    if annotation is str:
        return "str"
    if annotation is bool:
        return "bool"
    if annotation is int:
        return "int"
    if annotation is float:
        return "float"
    origin = typing.get_origin(annotation)
    if origin is typing.Union:
        args = [a for a in typing.get_args(annotation) if a is not type(None)]
        if len(args) == 1:
            return _declared_kind(args[0])
    return ""


def _hint_for(cls: Any, field: str) -> Any:
    """The annotation for one field, or None when the model declares none."""
    for name, annotation in typing.get_type_hints(cls).items():
        if name == field:
            return annotation
    return None

COPY alembic.ini ./alembic.ini

# STORAGE_PATH is declared here explicitly, and it is exactly where the Store
# gate mounts its volume: /data. It is the single persistence root (the SQLite
# file, or the WAL/SHM files beside it) and /health reports it fail-closed, so a
# deployment that mounts the volume anywhere else is a 503 rather than a silent
# loss of the winery's records on the next deploy.
ENV STORAGE_PATH=/data

# Create the storage root and hand it to the unprivileged service user BEFORE
# switching to that user, so a fresh volume mounted at STORAGE_PATH starts with
# the right ownership and the service never needs root to write its own data.
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 --shell /usr/sbin/nologin winery \
 && mkdir -p "$STORAGE_PATH" \
 && chown -R winery:winery "$STORAGE_PATH"
USER winery

EXPOSE 8000

# Never a 200-regardless probe. /health is fail-closed -- process, the
# persistent disk at STORAGE_PATH, the database app.db selects, and Alembic at
# head -- and answers 503 when any of them is down, so this reports the failure
# instead of hiding it. $PORT is read, not hardcoded: a runtime that injects
# PORT would otherwise leave a healthy container permanently "unhealthy".
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --start-period=30s --retries=3 \
    CMD python3 -c "import os,sys,urllib.request; port=os.environ.get('PORT') or '8000'; r=urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:'+port+'/health', timeout=2); sys.exit(0 if r.status==200 else 1)"

# Serve on ${PORT:-8000}. Shell form on purpose: the runtime's PORT must
# interpolate. Migrations are applied by the app's own startup (app.main:app's
# lifespan runs upgrade_head against the persistent disk) before the first
# request is served, so boot refuses rather than serving a schema behind head.
CMD uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8000}

One platform for a family money-transfer business: fermentation tanks, barrel inventory across
two cellars, harvest scheduling by sugar readings, wine club shipments, the lot
